Name of the Surah

• It is called At-Tawbah (Repentance), because the word "tawbah" (repentance) is mentioned and repeated in it, and because it contains the account of Allah's acceptance of the repentance of the three Companions who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk, may Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased.

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• Discussion of the rulings concerning the treaties between the Prophet ﷺ and the polytheists, and what follows from them regarding the states of war and peace, and the explanation of the rulings on fulfilling and breaking covenants, and the affirmation of disassociation (bara'ah) from the polytheists, and the lifting of protection from their persons and property.

• Declaration of war against the People of the Book until they give the jizyah (the tax levied on non-Muslim subjects under Muslim rule), and censure of what the rabbis (ahbar) and monks (ruhban) introduced into their religion of false beliefs, and the explanation of their greed for wealth, and that they are not far removed from the people of polytheism.

• Explanation of the sanctity of the Sacred Months, and the nullification of what the Arabs used to do in the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) of moving some months forward or postponing them according to their desires.

• Urging the Muslims to hasten to answer the call to fight in the cause of Allah, in hardship and in ease, and exhorting them to support the Prophet ﷺ, and that if they do not support him, Allah is his Supporter, and reminding them of Allah's victory for His Messenger ﷺ when He saved him from the plotting of the polytheists during the incident of the Hijrah (migration), and of His victory for him on the day of Hunayn.

• Praise of the Battle of Tabuk and allusion to the preparations for it, censure of the hypocrites who were sluggish, of those who made excuses and sought permission to stay behind without a valid excuse, and of those who discouraged others from going out to fight; and the praise of the expedition and its army, and mention of those whom Allah forgave among those who stayed behind from it.

• Exposing the methods of the hypocrites and their discouragement of the believers, where their characteristics are mentioned one after another: the Surah mentions their harm to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, their false oaths, their enjoining of evil and forbidding of good, their lying in their covenants, and their mockery of the weak among the believers, and it leaves them no veil except that it tears it away.

• Contrasting the characteristics and recompense of the people of disbelief and hypocrisy with their opposites among the believers and their recompense, and drawing attention to the virtue of Abu Bakr, the virtue of the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers), and alluding to the virtue of the Mosque of Quba and the Mosque of the Messenger ﷺ.

• Encouragement to give charity, to repent to Allah, and to do righteous deeds, and the command to seek understanding of the religion (fiqh) and to spread Islam.

• Allah's favor upon the Muslims in sending among them a Messenger from among them, endowed with qualities that contain every good for them, such as mercy and compassion; as an incentive for them to follow him and to adopt his noble manners ﷺ.

[Tafsir]

This is a declaration of disassociation from Allah and His Messenger, and a proclamation of the cancellation of the treaties that existed between the Muslims and the polytheists.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 2:

So travel freely in the land for four months, O polytheists, going wherever you wish, secure from the believers. And know that you will not escape punishment, and that Allah will humiliate the disbelievers and bring upon them shame in this world and the Fire in the Hereafter. This verse applies to those who had indefinite covenants without a fixed term, or to one who had a covenant of less than four months, which is then completed to four months for him, or to one who had a covenant and breached it.

A proclamation from Allah and His Messenger, and a warning to the people on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm an-Nahr) that Allah is free of the polytheists, and His Messenger is likewise free of them. So if you (polytheists) return to the truth and abandon your polytheism, it is better for you; but if you turn away from accepting the truth and refuse to enter the religion of Allah, then know that you will not escape the punishment of Allah. And warn, O Messenger, those who turn away from Islam of the painful punishment of Allah.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 4:

Excepted from the preceding ruling are the polytheists who entered into a covenant with you for a specified term, who have not breached the covenant, and who have not aided any of the enemies against you. Fulfill their covenant until its appointed end. Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him (al-muttaqun), who carry out what they were commanded and who guard against polytheism, treachery, and other acts of disobedience.

When the four sacred months during which you granted the polytheists safe conduct have passed, then declare war on the enemies of God wherever they may be, lay siege to them in their strongholds, and lie in wait for them along their routes. But if they repent of their disbelief, enter Islam, and adhere to its laws, including establishing prayer and paying zakat, then leave them alone, for they have become your brothers in Islam. Indeed, God is Forgiving toward whoever repents and turns back to Him, and Merciful toward them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 6:

And if any one of the polytheists whose blood and property have been made lawful (to be taken) asks you, O Messenger, for protection and seeks security, then grant him his request, so that he may hear the Noble Qur'an and become acquainted with its guidance. Then return him to his place of safety; and that is in order to establish the proof against him. That is because the disbelievers are a people ignorant of the realities of Islam, and so perhaps they will choose it once their ignorance is removed from them.

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 7:**

It is not fitting for the polytheists to have a covenant with Allah and His Messenger, except for those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram at the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah. So as long as they remain true to their covenant with you, remain true to them in the same way. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous who fulfill their covenants.

How could they have a covenant with God and His Messenger, when they are not faithful to it? Yet it is the commentary on verse 8 that reads:

The attitude of the polytheists is to keep their covenants only so long as the upper hand belongs to others. But if they feel strong against the believers, they do not respect kinship or covenant. So do not be deceived by what they show you when they fear you, for they tell you words with their tongues in order to win your approval, but their hearts refuse that, and most of them are rebellious against Islam and breakers of covenants.

They have exchanged the signs of Allah for the paltry goods of this world, so they turned away from the truth and barred those who desired Islam from entering it. Truly evil is what they have been doing, and wretched is their conduct.
Indeed, these polytheists are at war against faith and its people. So they give no weight to a believer's kinship or to his covenant, and their way is aggression and wrongdoing.

If they repent of worshipping other than Allah, utter the word of tawhid (monotheism), and adhere to the laws of Islam by establishing the prayer and giving the zakat, then they are your brothers in religion. And We make the verses clear, explaining them for a people who benefit from them.

If the polytheists break the treaties you have concluded with them, and openly revile the religion of Islam, then fight them, for they are the leaders of disbelief. They have no binding covenant and no pledge of protection, so that they may desist from their disbelief and their enmity toward Islam.

Do not hesitate to fight these people who broke their oaths, plotted to expel the Messenger from "Makkah," and were the first to attack you. Do you fear them, or fear meeting them in battle? Allah has more right to be feared by you, if you are truly believers.

O assembly of believers: fight the enemies of God. The Mighty and Majestic will punish them at your hands, will humiliate them through defeat and disgrace, will grant you victory over them, will make His word supreme, and will, through their defeat, heal your hearts, which have long been afflicted with sorrow and distress because of the plotting of these polytheists, and will remove the rage from the hearts of the believers. As for whoever among these obstinate people repents, God accepts the repentance of whomever He wills. God is All-Knowing of the sincerity of the repentant one, and All-Wise in His management, His craftsmanship, and His establishment of legislation for His servants.

O assembly of believers: fight the enemies of God. The Mighty and Majestic will punish them at your hands, will humiliate them through defeat and disgrace, will grant you victory over them, will make His word supreme, and will, through their defeat, heal your hearts, which have long been afflicted with sorrow and distress because of the plotting of these polytheists, and will remove the rage from the hearts of the believers. As for whoever among these obstinate people repents, God accepts the repentance of whomever He wills. God is All-Knowing of the sincerity of the repentant one, and All-Wise in His management, His craftsmanship, and His establishment of legislation for His servants.

It is part of Allah's way (sunnah) to test His servants. So do not suppose, O believers, that Allah will leave you without being tested, in order that Allah may make manifest to the creation (ʿilm ẓāhir) those who were sincere in their striving (jihad) and who did not take anyone other than Allah, His Messenger and the believers as intimate confidants (biṭānah) and allies (awliyāʾ). And Allah is All-Aware of all your deeds, and He will recompense you for them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 17:

It is not for the polytheists to maintain the houses of Allah, while they testify against themselves to their disbelief and associate partners with Him. Those polytheists—their deeds have become void on the Day of Resurrection, and their abode is eternal fire, where they will abide forever.

Only those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish the prayer, pay the zakat, and do not fear in Allah the blame of any blamer, tend to and maintain the houses of Allah. These maintainers are the ones guided to the truth.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 19:

Do you consider—O people—that what you do of giving drink to the pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Masjid is like the faith of one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in the way of Allah? ﴿They are not equal in the sight of Allah﴾. The state of the believers and the state of the disbelievers are not equal before Allah, because Allah does not accept any deed without faith. And Allah, glorified is He, does not guide to good deeds the people who wrong themselves through disbelief.

Those who believed in God, left the abode of disbelief seeking the abode of Islam, and spent their wealth and their lives in jihad (struggle in the way of God) to make the word of God supreme: these are greater in rank with God, and these are the ones who triumph through His good pleasure.

Indeed, those believers who emigrated have good tidings from their Lord of vast mercy and of good pleasure, after which there is no displeasure. Their destination is the Gardens of eternity, with lasting bliss.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 9, verse 22:

They will abide in those gardens forever, with no end to their stay or their enjoyment. This is the reward for the acts of obedience and righteous deeds they performed in their worldly life. Indeed, Allah the Exalted has a great reward for those who believe and do righteous deeds by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted according to His law, do not take your relatives—fathers, brothers, and others—as allies, revealing to them the secrets of the Muslims and consulting them in your affairs, as long as they remain upon disbelief, hostile to Islam. Whoever takes them as allies and conveys affection to them has disobeyed Allah, the Exalted, and wronged himself with a great wrong.

Say, [O Messenger], to the believers: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your relatives, the wealth you have acquired, the trade whose slowdown you fear, and the luxurious homes in which you dwell are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and jihad in His cause, then wait until Allah brings His punishment and vengeance upon you. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 9, verse 25:

Allah had indeed given you His victory in many battles, when you took the means and placed your trust in Allah. And on the day of the Battle of Hunayn you said, "We will not be defeated today for lack of numbers." But your large numbers deceived you and did not benefit you. The enemy prevailed over you, and you found no refuge in the vast earth, so you fled in defeat.

Then Allah sent down tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, so they stood firm. He reinforced them with hosts of angels that you did not see, gave them victory over their enemy, and punished those who disbelieved. Such is the punishment of Allah for those who turn people away from His religion and deny His Messenger.
Whoever turns back from his disbelief after that and enters Islam, then Allah accepts the repentance of whomever He wills among them, and forgives his sin. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

O believers, the polytheists are filth and impurity, so do not allow them to approach the Sacred Mosque after this ninth year of the Hijrah. And if you fear poverty because their trade with you will be cut off, then Allah will compensate you for it, and He will suffice you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed Allah is All-Knowing of your condition, All-Wise in the management of your affairs.

O Muslims: fight those disbelievers who do not believe in Allah, nor in the Resurrection and the Recompense, nor do they forbid themselves what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, nor do they adhere to the rulings of the Islamic Sharia, from among the Jews and the Christians, until they pay the jizya (poll tax) that you impose on them, handing it over with their own hands, humbled and subdued.

The Jews committed shirk against Allah when they claimed that Uzair is the son of Allah. The Christians committed shirk against Allah when they claimed that the Messiah is the son of Allah. This statement they invented from themselves, and in this they resemble the words of the polytheists before them. May Allah destroy the polytheists, all of them. How are they turned away from the truth to falsehood?

The Jews and the Christians have taken their scholars and their worshippers as lords who legislate rules for them, so they abide by those rules and abandon the laws of God. They have also taken the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, as a god and worshipped him, though God had commanded them all to worship Him alone, to the exclusion of anything else. He is the true God; there is no god but Him. He is exalted and holy above what the people of polytheism and misguidance fabricate.

The disbelievers want, by their denial, to extinguish the religion of Islam and to nullify the proofs of God and His evidences for His oneness, which Muhammad (ﷺ) brought. But God refuses except to complete His religion and make it prevail, and to raise His word, even though the deniers dislike that.

He is the One who sent His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) with the Qur'an and the religion of Islam, so that He might make it prevail over all other religions, even if the polytheists dislike the religion of truth, which is Islam, and its prevalence over the religions.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted according to His law, indeed many of the scholars of the People of the Book and their worshippers take people's wealth unjustly, such as through bribery and other means, and they prevent people from entering Islam and turn them away from the way of Allah. As for those who hoard wealth and do not pay its zakat (obligatory almsgiving), and do not give out the rights that are due from it, give them the good news of a painful punishment.

On the Day of Resurrection, pieces of gold and silver will be heated in the Fire. When their heat intensifies, the foreheads, sides, and backs of their owners will be branded with them. It will be said to them as a rebuke: "This is your wealth that you hoarded and withheld from the rights of Allah, so taste the painful punishment, because of your hoarding and withholding."

The number of months that make up the year, in God's decree and in what is recorded in the Preserved Tablet, is twelve months, from the day He created the heavens and the earth. Four of them are sacred (ḥurum): God forbade fighting in them (they are Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, al-Muharram, and Rajab). ﴿That is the upright religion﴾. ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾; this is because their sanctity is increased, and wronging oneself in them is graver than in other months, not that wronging is permitted in other months. ﴿And fight against all the polytheists just as they fight against you all﴾, and know that ﴿God is with those who are mindful of Him﴾ by His support and victory.

The commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 37:

Indeed, what the Arabs used to do in the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) of making four months of the year sacred was a matter of counting them, not of specifying them by the names of the months that Allah had made sacred. So they would postpone some of them or bring them forward, and in place of them they would make permissible whichever months they wished, according to their need for fighting. Indeed, that is an increase in disbelief, by which Satan leads astray those who disbelieve. They would make lawful the month whose sacredness they had postponed, in one year, and sacred it in another year, so that they would match the number of the four sacred months, and thus make lawful what Allah had made unlawful among them. ﴿Satan made their evil deeds seem attractive to them﴾. ﴿And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people to the truth and the right course﴾.

O you who have believed, what is wrong with you that when you are told, "Go forth in the cause of Allah," you sink down heavily to the earth? Have you been satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? But the enjoyment of this worldly life is little compared to the Hereafter, which Allah has prepared for the believing mujahideen; its bounty is abundant and lasting.

If you do not go forth, O believers, to fight your enemy, Allah will send down His punishment upon you, and He will bring in place of you a different people who will go forth when called upon, and who obey Allah and His Messenger. You will not harm Allah in the least by turning away from jihad; He is the Self-Sufficient, free of need of you, and you are the poor, in need of Him. What Allah wills always comes to pass without doubt, and Allah is capable of all things, including granting victory to His religion and His Prophet without you.

O assembly of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), if you do not go forth with him when he calls you to go forth, and do not help him, then Allah has already supported him and given him victory, on the day when the disbelievers, from Quraysh, expelled him from his homeland, Makkah, while he was the second of two (he and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him). They drove both of them to a cave in Mount Thawr in Makkah, and they remained there for three nights. When he said to his companion, Abu Bakr, seeing the fear he had for him: "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us," by His help and support. So Allah sent down tranquility upon the heart of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and aided him with soldiers that no one among mankind had seen, namely the angels. Thus Allah saved him from his enemy and humbled his enemies, and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah is the highest, and that is by elevating the status of Islam. Allah is Mighty in His dominion, Wise in the management of the affairs of His servants. In this verse there is a great virtue for Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him.

Go forth, O believers, to strive in the way of Allah, young and old, in hardship and in ease, whatever your condition, and spend your wealth in the way of Allah, and fight with your hands to raise high the word of Allah. That going forth and giving is better for you, in your present state and in your final outcome, than sluggishness, withholding, and staying behind. If you have knowledge of the virtue of jihad and its reward with Allah, then do what you have been commanded, and respond to Allah and His Messenger.

Allah, exalted is His majesty, rebuked a group of the hypocrites who sought permission from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to stay behind from the expedition of Tabuk, making clear that had their departure been toward a nearby, easily attained spoil and a journey without hardship, they would have followed you. But when they were called to fight the Romans at the borders of the land of al-Sham in the heat of summer, they shirked and stayed behind. They will soon offer excuses for their failure to go out, swearing by Allah that they were not able to do so, destroying themselves through lying and hypocrisy. And Allah knows that they are liars in the excuses they present to you.

May Allah pardon you, O Prophet, for what occurred from you of leaving what was preferable and more complete, which is your granting permission to the hypocrites to stay behind from jihad. Why did you grant these people permission to remain behind from the expedition, until those who were truthful in their excuses became clear to you, and you knew the liars among them in that matter?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 44:

It is not the way of those who believe in Allah, His Messenger and the Last Day to ask you, O Prophet, for permission to stay behind from striving in the cause of Allah with their lives and their wealth. Rather, this is the way of the hypocrites. And Allah is All-Knowing of those who fear Him and so guard themselves by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions.

Those who seek your permission to stay behind from striving (jihad) are only those who do not believe in God and the Last Day, and whose hearts are in doubt, so they waver in their doubt about the truth of what you have brought, O Prophet, of Islam and its laws.

If the hypocrites had truly intended to go out with you, O Prophet, to fight in jihad, they would have prepared for it with provisions and mounts. But Allah disliked their going out, so He made their departure burdensome for them, by His decree and predestination, even though He had commanded it by legislation. It was said to them: "Stay behind with those who sit back: the sick, the weak, and the women and children."

If the hypocrites had gone out with you, O believers, for jihad, they would only have added to you confusion and corruption, and would have hurried about among you spreading discord and hatred. They desire to cause you turmoil by discouraging you from jihad in the way of Allah. Among you, O believers, there are those who listen to them and carry your news to them. And Allah is All-Knowing of these hypocrites, the wrongdoers, and He will requite them for that.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 48:

They had already sought to cause turmoil for the believers and to turn them away from their religion and from the way of Allah, before the expedition of Tabuk, and to expose their affairs. O Prophet, they devised plots against you and turned matters around to nullify what you brought, as they did on the day of Uhud and the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq). They schemed against you until Allah's victory came, and He exalted His army and granted victory to His religion, while they were averse to it.

Among these hypocrites is one who asks your permission to stay behind from jihad, saying: "Do not put me to trial by exposing me to the temptation of women if I go out." Indeed, these hypocrites have fallen into the greatest trial, the trial of hypocrisy. And indeed, Hell encompasses the disbelievers in Allah and the Last Day, so not one of them will escape.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 50:

If good fortune and spoils come to you, O Prophet, the hypocrites are grieved; but if some harm befalls you, such as defeat or hardship, they say: "We had already taken our precaution by staying behind from Muhammad," and they turn away rejoicing in what they have done and in the misfortune that has befallen you.

Say, O Prophet, to these hesitant hypocrites, as a rebuke and reproach: "Nothing will befall us except what Allah has decreed for us and written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). He is our Protector against our enemies, and in Allah alone let the believers put their trust."

Say to them, O Prophet: "Do you await for us anything but one of the two good outcomes: martyrdom in the way of Allah, or victory over you? And we await for you that Allah afflict you with a punishment from Him, swift and destroying you, or by our hands, that we kill you. So wait, for we are waiting along with you, to see what Allah will do with each group of us and of you."

Say, [O Prophet], to the hypocrites: "Spend your wealth willingly or unwillingly, in whatever manner you choose; it will never be accepted from you, for you are a people who have departed from the religion of Allah and from obedience to Him."

The reason their expenditures were not accepted is that they concealed disbelief in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and denial of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). They do not come to the prayer except while lazy and reluctant, and they do not spend wealth except while unwilling. They neither hope for the reward of these obligatory acts nor fear punishment for abandoning them, because of their disbelief.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 55:

So let not their wealth or their children impress you, O Prophet. Allah only intends to punish them through these in the life of this world: through the toil of acquiring them and through the calamities that befall them, for they do not reckon that these are from Allah, and that their souls depart while they die upon their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger.

These hypocrites swear by Allah to you, O believers, falsely and baselessly, that they are truly of you, but they are not of you. Rather, they are a people who fear (you), so they swear (this) out of taqiyyah (precautionary dissimulation) toward you.

﴿If the hypocrites could find a refuge or a stronghold to protect them, or a cave in a mountain to shelter them, or a tunnel in the earth to save them from you, they would turn toward it at full speed.﴾

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 9, verse 58:

And among the hypocrites is one who finds fault with you regarding the distribution of the alms (al-sadaqat). If they receive a share of them, they are pleased and remain silent; but if they are not given any share of them, they become angry with you and criticize you.

If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them, and had said, "Allah is sufficient for us; Allah will grant us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger. Indeed, we turn our hopes toward Allah, that He may enrich us," and had said, "We desire that Allah expand provision for us and make us independent of charity and of people's charity." Had they done so, it would have been better for them and more beneficial.

Indeed, the obligatory zakat is given to the needy who own nothing, and to the poor who do not own what suffices them and meets their need; to those who collect it (al-sa'in, the zakat collectors); to those whose hearts are to be won over (mu'allafa al-qulub) by it, from among those whose Islam or strength of faith is hoped for, or whose benefit to the Muslims is hoped for, or by whom the evil of someone against the Muslims is averted; it is given for freeing slaves (riqab), including those who are bound by a contract of manumission (al-mukatabin); it is given to those burdened with debts (al-gharimin) for reconciling between people (li-islah dhat al-bayn), and to those whose debts have overwhelmed them, not due to corruption or extravagance, so that they have become unable to pay; to those who fight in the cause of Allah; and to the traveler who has run out of provisions. This distribution is an obligation that Allah has ordained and determined. Allah is All-Knowing of the interests of His servants, All-Wise in His management and His legislation.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 61:

Among the hypocrites are people who harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with their words, and they say: "He listens to everything that is said to him and believes it." Say to them, O Prophet: "He is an ear that listens to all good; he believes in Allah and trusts the believers in what they tell him, and he is a mercy to those who follow him and are guided by his guidance." As for those who harm the Messenger of Allah, Muhammad (ﷺ), in any kind of harm, they will have a painful, agonizing punishment.

The hypocrites swear false oaths and offer fabricated excuses in order to please the believers. Yet God and His Messenger have more right and are more worthy that they should seek to please them, through faith in them and obedience to them, if they are truly believers.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 63:

Do these hypocrites not know that the destination of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger is the Fire of Hell, where they will have everlasting punishment? That destination is disgrace and great humiliation. Among waging war against Allah and His Messenger is harming the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by reviling him and disparaging him. We seek refuge with Allah from that.

The hypocrites fear that a surah will be revealed concerning them, informing them of what they conceal in their hearts of disbelief. Say to them, O Prophet: Continue in your mockery and derision. Indeed, Allah will bring out into the open the reality of what you are wary of.

It's a translation of the tafsir passage on 9:65 for you. Here is the English:

If you were to question them, O Prophet, about what they said disparaging you and your Companions, they would surely say: "We were only chatting and joking without any real intent." Say to them, O Prophet: "Was it at Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking?"

Do not make excuses, O hypocrites; your excuses are of no use. You have disbelieved after your belief by this statement you mocked. If We pardon a group among you who sought forgiveness and were sincere in their repentance, We will punish another group because of their criminality in this wicked, sinful statement.

The hypocrites, men and women, are one kind: they profess faith outwardly while concealing disbelief within. They enjoin disbelief in God and disobedience to His Messenger, and forbid faith and obedience. They withhold their hands from spending in the way of God. They have forgotten God, so He has forgotten them, withdrawing His mercy from them, and so He has not granted them success in any good. Indeed, the hypocrites are those who have stepped outside of faith in God and His Messenger.

God has promised the hypocrites, both men and women, and the disbelievers that their final destination is the Fire of Hell, where they will abide forever. It is sufficient for them as a punishment for their disbelief in God. God has cast them out of His mercy, and for them is a lasting punishment.

Indeed, your deeds, O hypocrites, in mockery and disbelief, are like the deeds of the earlier nations who were superior to you in strength, wealth and children. They were content with the life of this world and enjoyed its shares and pleasures, and you, O hypocrites, have enjoyed your share of perishable desires just as those before you enjoyed their perishable shares. You plunged into falsehood against Allah just as those nations before you plunged. Those who are described with these traits are the ones whose good deeds have gone to waste in this world and the Hereafter, and they are the losers, for they sold the bliss of the Hereafter for their shares of this world.

Has there not come to these hypocrites the news of those who passed before them: the people of Noah, the 'Ad, the Thamud, the people of Abraham, the companions of Madyan (Midian), and the people of Lot, whose towns were overturned upon them, when their messengers came to them with clear proofs and the signs of Allah, and they denied them? So Allah sent His punishment upon all of them, as retribution for their evil deeds. Allah would never wrong them, but they were wronging themselves through their denial and opposition.

And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another: they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, they establish the prayer, they give the zakat (obligatory charity), they obey Allah and His Messenger, and they refrain from what they have been forbidden. Those, Allah will surely show them mercy; indeed Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.

Allah has promised the believing men and believing women, who believe in Allah and His Messenger, gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, whose bliss will never cease for them, and dwellings of good construction and pleasant abode in gardens of lasting residence. And approval from Allah is greater and more significant than the bliss they are in. That promise of the reward of the Hereafter is the great success.

O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers with the sword and against the hypocrites with the tongue and argument, and be stern with both groups. Their abode is Hell, and wretched is their destination.

The hypocrites swear by Allah that they said nothing [that would offend the Messenger and the Muslims]. Indeed, they are liars. They did say the word of disbelief and thereby apostatized from Islam, and they attempted to harm the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ), but Allah did not enable them to do that. The hypocrites found nothing to fault or criticize [in the Messenger], except that Allah, exalted is He, bestowed His favor upon them, enriching them through what He opened up for His Prophet (ﷺ) of good and blessing. So if these disbelievers return to faith and repentance, it is better for them; but if they turn away, or persist in their state, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world at the hands of the believers, and in the Hereafter with the Fire of Hell. They will have no rescuer to save them, nor any helper to ward off the evil of the punishment from them.

Among the hypocrites are some poor people who bind themselves by a covenant: "If Allah gives us wealth, we will surely give charity from it, and we will surely act as the righteous act with their wealth, and we will surely walk the path of righteousness."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 76:

When Allah gave them of His bounty, they were stingy about giving charity and spending their wealth on good causes, and they turned away while they were averse to Islam.

So the recompense for their deeds and their outcome was that He increased them in hypocrisy upon their hypocrisy, so that they cannot free themselves from it until the Day of Reckoning. That is because of their breaking the promise they had made to themselves, and because of their hypocrisy and their lying.

Did these hypocrites not know that Allah knows what they conceal within themselves and what they speak of in their gatherings of scheming and deceit, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen? So He will recompense them for their deeds, which He has recorded against them.

Along with the miserliness of the hypocrites, those who give charity are not spared from their harm. When the wealthy give large amounts of wealth, they find fault with them and accuse them of showing off (riya'), and when the poor give what is within their capacity, they mock them and say, in derision: ﴿What good is this charity of theirs?﴾ ﴿Allah mocks them, and for them is a painful, agonizing punishment.﴾

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 80:

Whether you ask forgiveness for them, O Messenger, or do not ask forgiveness for them, [it is the same:] God will never forgive them, however much you ask forgiveness for them and repeat it, because they disbelieved in God and His Messenger. And God, glory be to Him and exalted, does not guide to righteousness those who go outside His obedience.

The Easy Commentary (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) of King Fahd Complex on surah 9, verse 81:

Those who were left behind rejoiced at staying behind in "al-Madinah," defying the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they disliked striving with him in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Some of them said to others: "Do not go forth in the heat." The expedition of "Tabuk" took place at a time of intense heat. Say to them, O Messenger: "The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they knew that."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 9, verse 82:

Let these hypocrites, who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah in the Battle of Tabuk, laugh a little in their fleeting worldly life, and let them weep much in the Fire of Hell, as a recompense for what they used to earn in this world of hypocrisy and disbelief.

If Allah returns you, O Messenger, from your expedition to a group of the hypocrites who persist in hypocrisy, and they ask your permission to go out with you on another expedition after the expedition of Tabuk, then say to them: "You will never go out with me, nor will you fight with me against any enemy. You were content to sit back the first time, so sit back now with those who stayed behind from jihad with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

And do not ever pray (the funeral prayer), O Messenger, over any of the hypocrites who dies, nor stand at his grave to supplicate for him; for they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ), and died while they were defiant transgressors. This is a general ruling concerning everyone whose hypocrisy is known.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 85:

Do not let their wealth or their children impress you, O Messenger. Allah only intends to punish them with these in this world, by their enduring hardships on account of them, and by their dying in disbelief in Allah and His Messenger.

When a surah is sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ) commanding belief in Allah, sincerity toward Him, and striving (jihad) alongside the Messenger of Allah, the wealthy among the hypocrites ask you, O Messenger, for permission to stay behind, and they say: "Leave us with those who sit back, those unable to go out."

Those hypocrites were content for themselves with shame, namely that they sit in their homes with the women, the children, and those with excuses. Allah sealed their hearts because of their hypocrisy and their staying behind from jihad (striving in the cause of Allah) and from going out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the way of Allah. So they do not comprehend what is good for them and what leads them to guidance.

This is a passage from the commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 9, verse 88. It reads:

If these hypocrites stayed behind from the expedition, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers with him have striven with their wealth and their lives. For them there is victory and spoils in this world, and the Garden and honour in the Hereafter. It is they who are the successful.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 89:

Allah has prepared for them on the Day of Resurrection gardens beneath whose palaces and trees the rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great success.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 90:

A group of the Bedouin tribes came to [the city of] Madinah seeking excuses from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and explaining to him their weakness and their inability to go out for the military campaign. Others sat back without any genuine excuse, which they had made apparent, out of audacity toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ﴿Those among them who disbelieve will be afflicted with a painful punishment﴾: in this world, by killing and other things, and in the Hereafter, by the Fire.

There is no blame upon those with valid excuses, from among the weak, the sick, and the poor who do not possess the wealth with which to equip themselves for the expedition, for remaining behind, provided they are sincere toward Allah and His Messenger and act in accordance with His law. There is no fault in one who does good, of those whose excuse prevented them from fighting alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he is sincere toward Allah and His Messenger, from a path for which he would be punished or held accountable on account of it. And Allah is Forgiving toward the doers of good, Merciful to them.

Likewise, there is no blame upon those who came to you (O Prophet) seeking that you would provide them with mounts to carry them to jihad. You said to them: "I cannot find anything to carry you upon." So they turned away from you, their eyes overflowing with tears out of grief over what they had missed of the honor and reward of jihad, because they had nothing to spend and nothing to carry them had they gone out to fight in the way of Allah.

The blame and sin lie only with the wealthy who come to you, O Messenger, asking permission to stay behind. They are the hypocrites among the rich. They chose for themselves to sit with the women and those who have valid excuses. Allah has sealed their hearts with hypocrisy, so faith cannot enter them. They do not know the evil consequence of their staying behind from you and their abandoning jihad with you.

The commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 94:

﴿They will make excuses to you when you return to them.﴾ Those who stayed behind from fighting the polytheists, O believers, will make false excuses to you when you return from your campaign of Tabuk. Say to them, O Messenger: ﴿Make no excuses; we will not believe you. Allah has already informed us about your affairs.﴾ What you have said has shown us your lies. ﴿Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger.﴾ This is whether you repent of your hypocrisy or persist in it. ﴿And you will be shown to the people in this world.﴾ Then, after your death, ﴿you will be returned to the One from whom nothing of your inner and outer affairs is hidden,﴾ and He will inform you of all your deeds and repay you for them.

The hypocrites will swear to you by Allah, lying and making excuses, when you return to them from the campaign, so that you will leave them alone without questioning. So turn away from them and avoid them, disdaining them. Indeed, they are foul within, and their abode to which they retreat in the Hereafter is the Fire of Hell, as a recompense for what they used to earn of sins and transgressions.

This is the commentary on Surah 9, verse 96 from al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (King Fahd Complex):

"These hypocrites swear to you, O believers, falsely, so that you may be pleased with them. But if you are pleased with them, [then know that] since you do not know their lying, indeed Allah is not pleased with these people or others like them who persist in defiance (fisq) and in departing from the obedience of Allah and His Messenger."

The Bedouins, the dwellers of the desert, are more intense in disbelief and hypocrisy than the people of the settled towns, and that is due to their harshness, the hardness of their hearts, and their distance from knowledge, the scholars, and gatherings of admonition and remembrance of God. Therefore they are more deserving of not knowing the limits of the religion and what God has sent down of laws and rulings. And God is All-Knowing of the state of all of these, All-Wise in His management of the affairs of His servants.

Among the Bedouin are those who regard what they spend in the way of Allah as a loss and a penalty. They hope for no reward from it and expect it to bring them no protection from punishment, and they wait for misfortunes and calamities to befall you. But the evil turn of fortune will fall upon them, not upon the Muslims. And Allah is All-Hearing of what they say and All-Knowing of their corrupt intentions.

Among the Bedouins are those who believe in Allah, affirm His oneness, and believe in the Resurrection after death, and in reward and punishment. They seek Allah's reward for what they spend in struggle (jihad) against the polytheists, intending thereby to gain Allah's good pleasure and love, and they make it a means to obtain the supplication of the Messenger (ﷺ) for them. Indeed, these deeds bring them closer to Allah, and Allah will admit them into His Paradise. Surely Allah is Oft-Forgiving of what they have done of evil deeds, and Most Merciful toward them.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 9, verse 100:

Those who were foremost in becoming Muslims, first among the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun) and the Helpers (al-Ansar), and those who followed them in excellence in belief, statements and deeds, seeking the good pleasure of Allah, the Exalted: they are the ones with whom Allah is pleased because of their obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and they are pleased with Him because of the great reward He bestowed upon them for their obedience and faith. He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, their palaces and trees notwithstanding, abiding therein forever. That is the great success.

In this verse there is a declaration of the purity (tazkiyah) and the moral integrity (ta'dil) of the Companions (Sahabah), may Allah be pleased with them, and praise of them. For this reason, honouring them is one of the foundations of faith.

Among the Bedouins around Madinah are hypocrites (munafiqun), and among the people of Madinah are hypocrites who persisted in hypocrisy and increased in their rebellion against it, to the extent that their affair is hidden from you, O Messenger. We know them. We will punish them twice: with killing, captivity and disgrace in this world, and with the punishment of the grave after death. Then they will be returned on the Day of Resurrection to a great punishment in the Fire of Hell.

And others from the people of Medina and those around it, who acknowledged their sins, regretted them, and repented from them, mixed righteous deeds—which are repentance, remorse, acknowledgment of sin, and other righteous deeds—with another wrong deed—which is staying behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and other wrongful deeds. Perhaps Allah will guide them to repentance and accept it from them. Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving to His servants, Most Merciful to them.

Take, O Prophet, from the wealth of these repentant people, who mixed a righteous deed with another, bad one, a charity that purifies them from the filth of their sins and raises them from the abodes of the hypocrites to the abodes of the sincere believers. Pray for them for the forgiveness of their sins and seek forgiveness for them, for your prayer and your seeking forgiveness are a mercy and a source of tranquility for them. And Allah is All-Hearing of every supplication and utterance, All-Knowing of the conditions of His servants and their intentions, and He will recompense every doer for his deed.

Did these people who stayed behind from jihad, and others, not know that Allah alone accepts the repentance of His servants, accepts their charity and rewards them for it, and that Allah is the Ever-Returning (al-Tawwab) to His servants when they return to His obedience, and the Most Merciful (al-Rahim) toward them when they turn back to seek His pleasure?

And say, [O Prophet], to those who stayed behind from jihad: "Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger and the believers. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do." Within this is a warning and a threat for whoever persists in his falsehood and transgression.

And among those who stayed behind from you, O believers, in the expedition of Tabuk, are others who were deferred, so that God may decide concerning them what He decides. These are the ones who regretted what they had done, and they are: Murarah ibn al-Rabi', Ka'b ibn Malik, and Hilal ibn Umayyah. Either God will punish them, or He will pardon them. And God is All-Knowing of who deserves punishment or pardon, All-Wise in all His sayings and actions.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 107:

And [there are] the hypocrites who built a mosque for harm, disbelief in Allah, and division among the believers, and as a station for one who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before [that], namely Abu 'Amir al-Rahib (the monk), the wicked one. [They built it] so that some of them might pray in it while leaving the mosque of Quba' (Qubaʾ), where the Muslims pray, so that the Muslims would differ and split apart because of that. [They built it] in anticipation of one who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before, namely Abu 'Amir al-Rahib, the wicked one, so that it would be a place for plotting against the Muslims. The hypocrites will swear that they intended by building it nothing but good and kindness toward the Muslims, and extending [the mosque] for the weak and those unable to walk to the mosque of Quba'. But Allah bears witness that they are liars in what they swear to. The mosque was demolished and burned.

Do not stand (to pray) in that mosque ever, O Prophet. The mosque founded upon piety from the first day, which is the mosque of Quba', is more worthy that you stand in it for prayer. In it are men who love to purify themselves with water from impurities and filth, just as they purify themselves through abstaining from the forbidden and seeking forgiveness from sins and disobedience. And Allah loves those who purify themselves. And if the mosque of Quba' was founded upon piety from the first day, then the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is likewise, and even more so.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 109:

﴿Is one who founded his building upon taqwa of Allah and His pleasure better, or one who founded his building on the brink of a crumbling cliff about to collapse? So it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell.﴾ Whoever builds his structure upon fear of Allah, obedience to Him and seeking His pleasure is not equal to whoever builds his structure upon the edge of a crumbling pit, ready to fall, and so builds a mosque for harm, disbelief and dividing the Muslims. That led him into falling into the fire of Hell. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people who transgress His limits.

This is the commentary (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 9, verse 110. Here is the translation:

The building which the hypocrites have constructed to cause harm to the Masjid of Quba will continue to remain in their hearts as doubt and hypocrisy, until their hearts are torn apart, either by being killed or by dying, or by their regret reaching its utmost extent, and their repentance to their Lord and their fear of Him reaching its utmost extent. And Allah is All-Knowing of what these hypocrites hold of doubt and of what they intended in their building, All-Wise in the management of the affairs of His creation.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 111:

Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their selves and their wealth, in exchange for which they shall have Paradise and the bounties Allah has prepared therein. This is because they expend their souls and their wealth in striving against His enemies, to raise high His word and make His religion manifest. Thus they kill and are killed, a promise binding upon Him, true, in the Torah sent down to Moses (peace be upon him), the Gospel sent down to Jesus (peace be upon him), and the Qur'an sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ). And none is more faithful to his covenant than Allah, for those who fulfil what they have pledged to Allah. So rejoice, O believers, in the bargain you have made with Allah, and in what He has promised you of Paradise and His good pleasure. That bargain is the great success.

The attributes of these believers, to whom is the good news of entering Paradise, are: they are the repentant (al-tā'ibūn), who return from what Allah dislikes to what He loves and is pleased with; who have made worship sincerely for Allah alone and striven diligently in His obedience; who praise Allah for everything He tests them with, whether good or evil; who fast; who bow (rāki'ūn) in their prayer; who prostrate (sājidūn) in it; who enjoin people to do everything that Allah and His Messenger have commanded, and forbid them from everything that Allah and His Messenger have forbidden; who perform the obligations of Allah, and who stop at His command and prohibition; who stand firm in His obedience; and who keep within His limits. And give good news, O Prophet, to these believers who possess these attributes, of Allah's good pleasure and His Paradise.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 113:

It was not fitting for the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and the believers to ask Allah for forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were close relatives, after it became clear that they had died upon their polytheism, worshipping other than Allah and idols, and it became evident to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire (al-Jahim) because they died in polytheism. Allah does not forgive the polytheists, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with others in worship﴾, and as He, the Glorified, said: ﴿Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise﴾.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 114:

Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) asking forgiveness for his polytheist father was only due to a promise he had made to him, namely his saying: ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, He is ever gracious to me.﴾ Then, when it became clear to Ibrahim that his father was an enemy of Allah, and that admonition and reminder had no effect on him, and that he would die as a disbeliever, he abandoned him and abandoned asking forgiveness for him, and disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was greatly supplicating to Allah, and much forbearing toward the mistakes that proceeded from his people.

Allah would never misguide a people after He has guided them and granted them success, until He has made clear to them what they must beware of and what they need in the foundations and branches of the religion. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of everything. He has taught you what you did not know, made clear to you what benefits you, and established the proof against you by conveying His message to you.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 9, verse 116:

Indeed, Allah is the Owner of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. He has no partner in creation, in management, in worship, or in legislation. He gives life to whomever He wills and causes death to whomever He wills. You have no one other than Allah who takes charge of your affairs, and no helper who will support you against your enemy.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 117:

God granted His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) success in turning to Him in repentance and obeying Him. God also turned in mercy toward the Muhajirun (the Emigrants) who left their homes and their kinsfolk for the abode of Islam, and He turned in mercy toward the Ansar (the Helpers) of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) who went out with him to fight the enemies in the expedition of "Tabuk," in severe heat, and in a shortage of provisions and mounts. God indeed turned in mercy toward them after their hearts had nearly inclined away from the truth, so that they were inclining toward ease and rest. But God made them firm, strengthened them, and turned to them in mercy. Indeed, He is Most Compassionate and Most Merciful toward them, in this world and in the Hereafter. And of His mercy toward them is that He bestowed upon them the favor of repentance, accepted it from them, and kept them steadfast upon it.

Thus Allah turned in forgiveness to the three who were left behind from among the Ansar, namely Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya and Murarah ibn al-Rabi', who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and grieved greatly. So when the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness, through distress and remorse over their staying behind, and their own souls became constricted for them because of the anxiety that had befallen them, and they became certain that there is no refuge from Allah except with Him, Allah, glorified and exalted be He, granted them success in obedience and in returning to what pleases Him. Indeed, Allah is the Ever-Accepting of repentance toward His servants, the Most Merciful to them.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: comply with the commands of Allah and avoid His prohibitions in everything you do and everything you refrain from, and be with the truthful in their oaths and their covenants, and in every matter of their affairs.

It was not fitting for the people of Madinah, and for the Bedouins dwelling around them, to stay behind in their homes and dwellings, away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), nor to prefer their own ease over his, while the Messenger (ﷺ) was in hardship and toil. That is because whatever thirst, fatigue, or hunger they suffer in the path of Allah during their journey and their struggle, and whatever step they take that enrages the disbelievers, and whatever harm they inflict upon the enemies of Allah and their enemies, slaying or defeat, is recorded for them as a righteous deed, for all of it. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of those who do good.﴾ That is, those who do good in hastening to obey the command of Allah, and in fulfilling what is incumbent upon them of His right and the right of His creation.

They do not spend any amount, small or large, in the cause of Allah, nor do they cross any valley on their march with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his jihad, except that it is recorded for them as a reward for their deeds, so that Allah may repay them with the best of what they are repaid for their righteous deeds.

And it was not appropriate for the believers to all go out to fight their enemy. Likewise, it is not right for them all to stay behind. So why did not a group from every division go out for military expedition and struggle (jihad), such that sufficiency and the purpose are achieved through them? This is so that those who stay behind from fighting may gain understanding (yatafaqqahu) and know what new rulings have been introduced in the religion of God and what was revealed to His Messenger, and so that they may warn their people with what they have learned when they return to them, so that perhaps they will beware of the punishment of God by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 123:

O you who have believed Allah and His Messenger and acted according to His law, begin by fighting those disbelievers nearest to you, in order of proximity to the abode of Islam (Dar al-Islam), and let the disbelievers find in you harshness and severity. And know that Allah is with the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) through His support and His victory.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 9, verse 124:

When a surah of the Qur'an is sent down by Allah to His Messenger, among these hypocrites there are those who say, in denial and mockery: "Which of you has had his faith increased by this surah?" As for those who believed in Allah and His Messenger, the descent of the surah increased them in faith, through knowing it, reflecting upon it, believing in it, and acting by it. They rejoice in what Allah has given them of faith and certainty.

As for those who have hypocrisy and doubt about the religion of God in their hearts, the revelation of the surah increases them in hypocrisy and doubt, added to the hypocrisy and doubt they already had before. These people perished while they were deniers of God and His signs.

Do the hypocrites not see that Allah tests them every year, once or twice, with drought and hardship and by exposing what they conceal of hypocrisy? Yet even so, they do not repent of their disbelief and hypocrisy, nor do they take heed or remember through the signs of Allah that they witness.

When a surah is revealed, the hypocrites exchange glances with one another, in denial of its revelation, mockery and rage, because of what it contains of mention of their faults and deeds. Then they say: "Does anyone see you if you rise from the presence of the Messenger?" If no one sees them, they rise and leave his presence, peace and blessings be upon him, out of fear of exposure. Allah has turned their hearts away from faith, because they do not understand and do not reflect.

Surah 9, verse 128 in the Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar):

"There has certainly come to you, believers, a messenger from among yourselves. It grieves him that you suffer hardship and distress; he is eager for your faith and the welfare of your affairs, and toward the believers he is extremely kind and merciful."

If they turn away from faith in you, O Messenger, then say to them: ﴿Allah is sufficient for me﴾; He suffices me for all that concerns me. There is no deity worthy of worship except Him. In Him I place my trust, and to Him I have entrusted all my affairs, for He is my helper and supporter. He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne, and the Throne of the Most Merciful is the greatest of created things.
